Custom Chat photo selection introduces no second asset owner or image copy. Selection references use the Chat lifecycle; removing or withdrawing clearance from an asset prevents fresh selection metadata and further selected-task processing. Earlier submitted IDs remain immutable historical facts and cannot keep an otherwise removable photo alive. Current task upload source additionally stores immutable original handoff interaction ID and definition digest (or explicit null for direct uploads) in project_files and exact browser recovery metadata. This locator follows file custody, independently of Chat payload expiry/dismissal; it grants no retained interaction or media authority. Server-confirmed closure of an unreserved handoff can resolve browser recovery because new reservations are atomically refused after closure. Current originating-task inference may read only linked names/dimensions and upload/safety status under scoped read admission. Those explicit model-request/reply/summary copies follow existing AI and Chat retention; image bytes, object keys, file digests and unrelated uploads are excluded. Dismissal never clears a reserved upload or its unresolved operation.

classes.purpose: Customer-authorized provider access and durable credential revocation.
classes.currentRetention: Encrypted credentials retained for pending revocation until confirmed or expired; OAuth expiry cleanup. Account cascades can destroy revocation authority prematurely. Current source retains unresolved dispatched exchanges without automatic expiry, restricting account deletion and key activation; transient rotation guards exist only inside a transaction. Exact dispatch rejection/revocation receipts contain only bounded metadata and remain until account closure/independent retention reconciliation; a restored receipt alone grants no authority. GitHub refresh credentials use a separate encrypted purpose and RESTRICT references; access expiry or single-token revocation cannot delete their pending grant custody. Numeric GitHub identity is bound once from the exact issued token's authenticated lookup and retained independently of later connections; missing lookup evidence remains unknown. This metadata is not revocation proof. Reviewed app-grant revocation can remove the exact matched ciphertext only after a directly acknowledged, atomically saved 204. Immutable review/outcome metadata remains; unknown effects and unidentified grants stay held. The shared customer renderer and Chat controls have local and bounded deployed test acceptance (Chat connection release 5dfb930c, October 3). Real provider consent/permissions/revocation and customer/device acceptance remain pending. Current source stores immutable connection_chat_links alongside OAuth start in one transaction. They contain provider, hashed state, original owner/session ID, interaction ID/digest and timestamps only. They survive one-time OAuth state consumption/replacement and card dismissal for return navigation; they expire at the originating card seven-day retention deadline and hourly Chat maintenance removes up to 100 expired links. Account/interaction/project deletion cascades them. A return requires the exact current owner/session and current project ownership. Consumed, expired or replayed OAuth state never regains exchange authority. Dismissal or link expiry does not delete already-started credential custody. No credential, verifier, approval or redirect URL is copied into Chat. This locator grants no restored authority. Task-scoped status uses a transient metadata fingerprint and existing saved-status readers after inference. Only provider-name locators enter task context; the server reply follows existing Chat retention and is excluded from later model context. No credential, provider login or fingerprint is persisted in that reply, and no new data class or authority is introduced.
classes.proposedRetention: Cancel callbacks/new consent on closure; revoke credentials before deleting ciphertext/key access. Keep unresolved revocation work in isolated minimal closure records, without preserving unrelated customer content.
classes.deletionAuthority: Customer disconnect/closure authorizes access revocation, not deleting repositories/zones. Operator reconciles failed revocation.
classes.exportPolicy: Provider names, customer connection status and selected resource metadata only. Never tokens, ciphertext, PKCE verifier, auth state or encryption material. Exclude OAuth Chat-return locators; the ordinary Chat lifecycle owns interaction history.

readers: Exact current owner/credential-admitted provider adapters; narrow revocation worker retains only cleanup custody

processors: OAuth PKCE/token exchange, current scoped provider calls and recorded read-only uncertain recovery; no credential in model context
remainingExposure: Authorized Worker plus the retained exact key can decrypt tokens. Local fenced rotation does not establish independent key custody, permitted restore admission or deployed cutover. Unknown provider outcomes retain recovery obligations.
protection.rationale: Database-only exposure must not supply reusable provider access; extend the existing authenticated vault, not customer unlock UX.
